reference.source: Firestein & Kelley's Textbook of Rheumatology / Rook's Textbook of Dermatology
clinicalPearls: A rare cutaneous mucinosis presenting with widespread firm, waxy papules and induration, often in a linear arrangement over the trunk and limbs
Involvement of the glabella and ears with deep longitudinal furrowing can produce a leonine facies, and the 'Shar-Pei sign' describes redundant folds
Almost always associated with a monoclonal gammopathy, characteristically an IgG lambda paraprotein
Despite the paraprotein, there is usually no overt myeloma, and the skin disease dominates the picture
Systemic involvement can affect the central nervous system (the dermato-neuro syndrome), heart, oesophagus, and muscles, occasionally with fatal outcomes
Histology shows dermal mucin deposition, fibroblast proliferation, and fibrosis, distinguishing it from systemic sclerosis
Intravenous immunoglobulin is a mainstay of treatment, with other systemic immunomodulatory options for resistant disease
reference.pathophysiology: Scleromyxoedema is a generalised form of lichen myxoedematosus characterised by deposition of mucin (glycosaminoglycans) in the dermis together with proliferation of fibroblasts and increased collagen. It is almost invariably associated with a monoclonal gammopathy, usually IgG lambda, though the paraprotein's precise pathogenic role is unclear and disease activity does not track paraprotein levels. Circulating factors are thought to stimulate dermal fibroblasts to overproduce mucin and collagen, and the process may extend to internal organs, producing systemic and, in the dermato-neuro syndrome, central neurological complications.
additionalInvestigations: Skin biopsy showing dermal mucin deposition, fibroblast proliferation, and fibrosis
Serum protein electrophoresis and immunofixation to detect the monoclonal paraprotein
Serum free light chains and quantitative immunoglobulins
Bone marrow examination to assess the plasma cell clone and exclude myeloma
Investigations for systemic involvement (cardiac, oesophageal, neurological) as clinically indicated
Thyroid function tests to exclude mimicking causes of skin thickening
redFlags: Acute encephalopathy, seizures, or coma suggesting the dermato-neuro syndrome
Cardiac or oesophageal involvement causing functional compromise
Progression of the paraprotein towards multiple myeloma
Rapidly progressive skin induration limiting mobility
reference.prognosis: Scleromyxoedema is a chronic, often progressive disorder; skin disease may respond to intravenous immunoglobulin and immunomodulation, but systemic and central nervous system involvement, particularly the dermato-neuro syndrome, can be life-threatening.
pitfalls: Mistaking it for systemic sclerosis and missing the associated paraprotein
Failing to perform serum protein electrophoresis and immunofixation in a patient with unexplained waxy skin induration
Assuming absence of myeloma excludes significant disease
Tracking treatment response by paraprotein level rather than clinical activity
